chunks: Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:

If you do not know whether you prayed two rakʿahs or four, and your doubt does not incline to anything, then recite the tashahhud and give salām, then pray two rakʿahs and four sajdahs, reciting in them Umm al-Kitāb. Then recite the tashahhud and give salām. If you had only prayed two rakʿahs, these two will complete the four; and if you had prayed four, these two will be supererogatory.

key_terms.تَدْرِ: to know or determine with certainty
key_terms.سَجَدَاتٍ: prostrations performed within the two rakʿahs
key_terms.سَلِّمْ: give the salām ending the prayer
key_terms.وَهْمُكَ: your doubtful impression or uncertain assumption

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they doubt whether they prayed two or four rakʿahs?
ai.summary: This hadith gives the ruling for one who doubts between two and four rakʿahs and has no stronger assumption toward either side. The person completes the prayer with tashahhud and salām, then performs two precautionary rakʿahs so that, if the original prayer was short, it is completed, and if it was already complete, the added rakʿahs count as supererogatory prayer.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1015 - Al-Halabi narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) that He said:

"If you do not know whether you prayed two rak'ahs or four, and your doubt does not lead you to any conclusion, then perform the tashahhud and give the salaam, then pray two more rak'ahs with four prostrations. In them, recite Al-Fatiha.
Afterward, perform the tashahhud and give the salaam. If you had prayed only two rak'ahs, then these will complete the four. But if you had prayed four, then these two will be considered as voluntary (nawafil)."
